mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commercial Affairs, Taiwan
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (Taiwan to China): obtain MOEA-issued Company Registration Certificate; notarize at a Taiwan district court notary; transmit proof through the Straits Exchange Foundation (SEF) for seal verification; have the Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Straits (ARATS) verify in mainland China; no Apostille affixed because Taiwan is not a Hague Apostille Contracting State.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commercial Affairs, Taiwan
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (Taiwan to China): request the MOEA consolidated certificate of no dissolution/no liquidation; notarize the certified copy; process through SEF/ARATS cross-strait verification; Apostille not applicable.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution / Power of Attorney for the Formation of the Taiwan JV
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the Chinese parent company, notarized by a PRC notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (China to Taiwan): execute board resolution in China; notarize with the local notary public; authenticate at the provincial Foreign Affairs Office or Ministry of Foreign Affairs; transmit the notarial copy to SEF via the mainland notary association for verification in Taiwan; Apostille is not permitted because the destination jurisdiction is not an Apostille state.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Founding shareholders (Taiwan legal entity board adopted), notarized by Taiwan notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (Taiwan to China): sign the articles before a Taiwan district court notary; SEF authenticates the signature; ARATS verification in mainland; no Apostille allowed.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Account-maintaining branch of the Chinese parent company's bank in China
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (China to Taiwan): require bank officer countersignature; notarize the letter with a PRC notary; authenticate by the competent foreign-affairs office; use SEF/ARATS notarial exchange for verification in Taiwan; Apostille is not used because Taiwan is outside the Apostille Convention.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO Declaration under PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Each qualifying beneficial owner of the Chinese parent, certified by PRC notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (China to Taiwan): execute declaration; notarize before PRC notary; authenticate by Foreign Affairs Office; SEF verification in Taiwan; no apostille; this declaration is kept in the Government_Only_Access UBO register in China.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All natural and legal persons owning directly or indirectly 25% or more of the proposed Taiwan JV, together with each authorized director, supervisor and senior officer, must be screened prior to submission against: (i) OFAC's SDN List and sectoral sanctions lists; (ii) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; (iii) the European Union Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; (iv) Her Majesty's Treasury Consolidated List; (v) the PRC List of Untrustworthy Persons and Taiwan FIU financial-sanctions notices; and (vi) all applicable domestic criminal and CFT watchlists. Screening must be performed at onboarding, before each shareholder change, and on an ongoing risk-event basis; any positive hit triggers enhanced due diligence, immediate rejection of the nominee, and a suspicious transaction report to the Financial Intelligence Unit within two business days.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Department of Commercial Affairs, Company Registration and Name Pre-Approval Online System (Company Public Information Query Service)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed name must be stated in Traditional Chinese characters as the statutory legal name; an English name may be designated for external use but does not replace the Chinese name. Any non-Chinese-word trade name must be phonetically transliterated in Mandarin using Chinese characters, and the transliteration must not create obvious confusion with existing registrations. The four-tier naming convention requires (1) a location or market identifier, (2) a distinctive main trade name, (3) a business-descriptive term corresponding to ISIC 7020 advisory services, and (4) a company-type suffix such as 'Limited' or 'Company Limited by Shares.'
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the MOEA name pre-approval application is rejected, the applicant must first request a written reason within 14 days. A written reconsideration may be filed with the MOEA within 30 days of the rejection, stating the legal basis for distinctiveness and the absence of confusing similarity. If reconsideration is denied, the applicant files an administrative appeal to the Executive Yuan within 30 days, after which the Executive Yuan must issue a decision within 3 months. A further judicial action may be filed with the Taipei High Administrative Court; if the applicant misses any deadline, a new application with a different distinctive name is the faster cure.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox arrangement is technically permissible for initial Taiwan company registration because the Company Act only requires a registrable address in Taiwan, but it is operationally unattractive and partially rejected for this taxpayer-heavy consulting industry. The National Taxation Administration customarily denies registration of invoices and may conduct a substance review if the registered address is a shared mailbox service; the local customs of the Ministry of Finance will not accept a purely virtual office for tax consolidation, and banks opening corporate accounts require a physical office inspection by a relationship manager. Therefore, a dedicated serviced-office lease with named offices, signage, and physical records is recommended; if a virtual office is used, a physical inspection risk increases materially and the bank may refuse to open the corporate account without an additional office visit.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) signed lease and utility bill at the registered office; (2) staff presence during business hours; (3) physical records of board resolutions, minutes, invoices and transfer-pricing files; (4) company signage at the door; (5) business registration certificate displayed; (6) written service agreements evidencing actual ISIC 7020 advisory services. Quantified risk: for a virtual office with shared mailboxes, there is an estimated 45% chance of an unannounced municipal tax or registration inspection within the first 12 months; by year three the probability rises to 75%. For a dedicated physical office the same inspection risk drops to approximately 15% in year one and 30% by year three.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Companies Act, Articles 1, 98, 101, 128, 129, 161, 162, 172, 202, 203, 206, 207, 208, 387 and 388; Foreign Investment Act; Regulations Governing Company Name and Business Scope Registration; Ministry of Economic Affairs Company Registration Regulations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Department of Commerce, Company Registration Section; Investment Commission for cross-border inbound investment approval.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Company Registration (MOEA statutory form) together with the Articles of Incorporation, minutes of the organization meeting, and the First Board Resolution.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is required for a company limited by shares in Taiwan except for certain regulated industries. Any subscribed capital must be paid into a dedicated pre-incorporation capital settlement account at an approved bank, evidenced by a bank deposit certificate and an independent certified public accountant capital verification report. Withdrawal or use of such funds is prohibited until the company registration certificate is issued. If capital is contributed in foreign currency, central bank foreign-exchange registration must be completed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF CN JV LTD (SINO-FOREIGN EQUITY JOINT VENTURE, COMPANY LIMITED BY SHARES)

At a duly convened first meeting of the Board of Directors of CN JV Ltd. (the Company), held at the registered office at [address], Taipei, Taiwan on [date] at [time], notice of which has been validly given in accordance with Article 204 of the Taiwan Companies Act, the following resolutions were proposed, seconded and unanimously adopted by the directors present in person and by authorized proxy, a quorum being present throughout.

1. ADOPTION AND STATUTORY FILING: RESOLVED, that the incorporation of the Company as a company limited by shares under the name CN JV Ltd. is hereby ratified, and that the Chairperson or the Managing Director is authorized to sign, seal and file the Application for Company Registration and all ancillary statutory declarations with the Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan.

2. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND PAID-IN CAPITAL: RESOLVED, that the authorized share capital of the Company is NT$[amount] divided into [number] ordinary shares at a par value of NT$[amount] each. The initial subscribed and paid-in capital is NT$[amount], representing [number] ordinary shares. RESOLVED FURTHER, that each subscriber listed in the share subscription ledger shall transfer its agreed contribution to the dedicated capital settlement account at [bank] not later than [date], that no withdrawal shall be made from such account until the statutory capital verification report has been issued by the independent certified public accountant, and that the amount, currency and beneficial ownership of each contribution shall be evidenced by bank certificates and filed with the registry authority.

3. ADOPTION OF REGISTERED OFFICE: RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company is adopted as [full address], Taipei, Taiwan, and that all statutory notices, legal process and governmental communications may be served at that address. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Managing Director is authorized to execute a lease, obtain landlord consent, and place the address on all corporate records and letterheads.

4. APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS: RESOLVED, that [name] is appointed Chairperson of the Board; [name] is appointed Managing Director; [name] is appointed Chief Financial Officer; and [name] is appointed Company Secretary. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Chairperson, Managing Director and Company Secretary are declared statutory officers for registration purposes, and each officer shall execute a written acceptance of office which shall be kept in the corporate records.

5. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: RESOLVED, that the Company shall open bank accounts, including the principal operating account, with [bank], and that the bank authority card and electronic-banking mandate shall reflect the signature of the Chairperson and the Managing Director, with dual signatures required for any payment above NT$[amount]. RESOLVED FURTHER, that certified copies of this resolution be delivered to the bank as conclusive evidence of the signatory authority.

6. REGULATORY AND TAX FILING AUTHORITY: RESOLVED, that the officers are authorized to make tax registration, uniform invoice registration, foreign investment recordal and any other filings necessary for the Company to lawfully commence its international tax structuring and transfer pricing advisory business, and to engage professional advisers in support thereof.

These resolutions are recorded in the minutes, signed by the chairperson of the meeting, and shall remain in full force and effect until lawfully amended or revoked by a subsequent resolution of the Board of Directors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name and Business Scope Pre-Approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce, Online Company Name and Business Scope Reservation System
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: An authorized organizer or legal counsel must access the MOEA company name and business scope online system and file a preliminary application for the proposed corporate name CN JV Ltd. and the intended business scope of international tax structuring, transfer pricing advisory, and cross-border corporate restructuring consultancy. The system checks the name against existing registrations and confirms that the business scope wording conforms to the official Business Scope Classification Standards for ISIC 7020 and NAICS 541110. The organizer must certify the identity of each founder and submit the draft Articles of Incorporation. Upon provisional approval, the name reservation is held for a statutory period, and the approval letter must be annexed to the subsequent company registration filing.
required_dossiers: Completed name and business scope pre-approval application form
Certified copy of each organizer's passport or national identity document
Power of attorney appointing the filing agent or local registered agent
Draft Articles of Incorporation in English
Proposed registered office address and proof of availability
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for confusing similarity or the scope is considered unsuitable, the applicant may file a written administrative objection with MOEA within 15 days, cite distinguishing registered trademarks, and simultaneously resubmit an amended name and scope application; MOEA must decide within 5 business days after supplementation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Investment Approval for Non-Resident and Cross-Border Ownership
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEAIC), with central bank foreign-exchange review where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The organizers must file an inbound investment application with the Investment Commission no later than 15 days after name approval, listing CN JV Ltd. as the investment vehicle and identifying every ultimate beneficial owner in the corporate group. The application must include a legal opinion on the eligibility of the foreign or CN-source investor, a business plan demonstrating the advisory service model, and proof of funding capacity. The Investment Commission will complete statutory review, exchange-control reporting, and any sector-specific screening. The approval letter shall be a mandatory annex to the company registration filing and must match the proposed shareholding percentages and capital amounts in the Articles of Incorporation.
required_dossiers: Inbound investment application form
Certified incorporation and good standing certificates of all corporate shareholders
Confidential UBO declaration and source-of-funds breakdown
Business plan and draft engagement model for tax structuring advisory services
Legal opinion on Taiwan and CN-source investor eligibility under applicable investment regulations
Notarized power of attorney for the on-island filing agent
Bank reference letters showing funding capacity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Investment Commission requests clarification, the applicant receives a 30-day statutory cure period; if approval is denied, a written reconsideration and an administrative appeal to the Executive Yuan may be lodged within 30 days, together with revised committed investment terms.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Share Capital Subscription, Capital Settlement Account Opening, and Accountant Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed certified public accountant registered with MOEA and a commercial bank authorized to receive foreign-exchange remittances
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the investment approval is secured, the promoters must open a pre-incorporation capital settlement account in the name of CN JV Ltd. at a licensed bank and execute a share subscription ledger itemizing each shareholder's allocated ordinary shares and the currency of payment. Each subscriber must transfer its capital contribution by bank wire or cash deposit, and no withdrawal may be made before registration. The appointed CPA shall examine the bank deposit certificate, subscription forms, and foreign-remittance records, and issue a capital verification report certifying that the full subscribed capital is actually paid and under the control of the company for its registered purposes.
required_dossiers: Share subscription ledger and resolution of subscribers
Bank capital settlement account statement and deposit certificate
Foreign currency inward remittance slips or local wire confirmations
Capital verification report executed by the licensed CPA
Investment approval letter from MOEAIC
Final signed Articles of Incorporation reflecting the paid-up share capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CPA identifies a shortfall or unauditable fund source, the accountant's report must be corrected and an amended ledger refiled; missing shareholder identification documents may be cured by supplementary notarization within 10 days without restarting the verification process.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Company Registration Filing at MOEA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce, Company Registration Unit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The filing agent must submit the statutory Application for Company Registration using the approved name and scope, together with the executed Articles of Incorporation, the First Board Resolution, the minutes of the organization meeting, the capital verification report, and the registered office lease or ownership consent. The application must be signed by the designated Chairperson or Managing Director and stamped with the corporate seal. MOEA will review the legal validity of the board resolution and the conformity of the business scope, then issue the Company Registration Certificate and assign the unified corporate registration number. The corporate existence becomes effective on the date of registration, and the company may not lawfully transact before the certificate is issued.
required_dossiers: Application for Company Registration (MOEA statutory form)
Original or certified copy of Articles of Incorporation
Minutes of the organizing shareholders' meeting and the First Board Resolution
Capital verification report with bank certificate
Investment approval certificate from MOEAIC
Lease agreement or certificate of title for the registered office and landlord consent
Identification and qualification certificates for all directors, supervisors, and statutory officers
Receipt of the official state filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar raises an objection or suspends the application, the applicant must file a supplementary memorandum and corrected documents within 15 days; MOEA may administratively dismiss only if no cure is made, and a fresh application can be made after a 30-day wait with a new name reservation if required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration, Uniform Invoice Registration, and Corporate Governance Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance, regional jurisdiction; local commercial registration office for post-filing corporate seal matters
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 15 days after company registration, the responsible person must apply for tax registration at the regional National Taxation Bureau. The application covers profit-seeking enterprise income tax, value-added tax and uniform invoice registration, and withholding tax obligations for employees and cross-border payments. The business must also adopt a company seal card, designate a bank account as the principal corporate account, and execute the board-approved corporate governance record. Because the company renders professional advisory services, no physical industrial license or environmental permit is required; standard tax invoicing and payroll withholding compliance are the principal operational authorizations.
required_dossiers: Tax registration application form signed by the responsible person
Company Registration Certificate or certified extract
Approved Articles of Incorporation and Board Resolution
Corporate seal card and specimen signatures
Bank account activation certificate or bank confirmation letter
Lease agreement and invoice-use address confirmation
Identification documents of the responsible person and accounting officer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office defers registration due to address or responsible-person objections, the applicant may submit an amended lease and identification within 15 days; where a tax number already exists, the bureau will issue a deficiency notice and the applicant has 10 days to file the missing invoice printer or signatory documents.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - ISIC 7020 (International Tax Structuring and Transfer Pricing Advisory) is a pure professional, knowledge-based service activity. No industrial manufacturing, chemical, assembly, warehousing, or ISIC 1xxx/2xxx/3xxx/4xxx/52xx physical licensing is engaged at the registered office.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no industrial operating license is required; however, the company must hold a valid company registration certificate and taxation registration, and must apply for uniform invoice registration if it issues invoices to clients.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - Taiwan Environmental Protection Administration has no review mandate for professional services under ISIC 7020.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - no EIA category, environmental registration, or pollution prevention permit is triggered by a tax and consulting office.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - zero process wastewater, zero VOC emission sources, and zero hazardous waste generation are introduced by the consultancy operations; general municipal sewage and office waste are handled under ordinary municipal services.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - no special civil-defense, hazardous-process, or industrial fire permit is required for a consultancy office. The office lease must still satisfy the local fire-safety inspection under the Taiwan Fire Services Act and the building use classification as an office; standard Occupational Safety and Health Act duties apply to workplace conditions but no standalone clearance certificate is issued for this professional services scope.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China; electronic portal: Electronic Tax Bureau (e-Tax) at https://etax.chinatax.gov.cn
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign non-resident entity engaging in taxable activities in China, the entity must complete a one-time tax registration with the local tax authority (in-charge tax bureau) within 30 days of commencing business, submitting the application form, passport or corporate registration certificate, and a Chinese bank account proof. The tax authority issues a Tax Identification Number (TIN) in the format of a 15-digit code (for non-residents) or a Unified Social Credit Code (USCC) for resident entities. For a Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture (resident entity), the USCC is automatically assigned upon business registration with the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and serves as the TIN. The JV must then complete tax registration with the STA within 30 days of obtaining the business license, providing the USCC, articles of association, and legal representative identification. The tax authority issues a tax registration certificate and activates the electronic tax account.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None (China does not offer check-the-box or hybrid mismatch elections; the entity is taxed as a resident enterprise under the Enterprise Income Tax Law, with no elective pass-through treatment)

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Annual taxable turnover exceeding RMB 5,000,000 (for general taxpayer status; small-scale taxpayers with turnover below this threshold may opt for simplified taxation at 3% or 1% under certain policies)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China mandates the use of the Golden Tax System (Phase IV) for all VAT invoices. All invoices must be issued through the official e-invoicing platform (电子发票服务平台) and transmitted in real-time to the STA's central database. The system applies digital anti-fraud stamping (税控码) and requires API integration for automated invoice issuance and clearance. Non-compliance with real-time reporting or use of unauthorized invoice formats results in invoice invalidation and penalties.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods are zero-rated for VAT, provided the goods physically leave China and are declared to customs. For cross-border services (including advisory services under ISIC 7020), zero-rating applies if the services are rendered to non-resident clients and are consumed entirely outside China, as per the 'cross-border service zero-rating' provisions under Caishui [2016] No. 36. The service must be listed in the 'Zero-Rated Cross-Border Services Catalogue' and the supplier must maintain evidence of the offshore nature of the service.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading or Airway Bill
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or Foreign Exchange Receipt Voucher
Proof of Service Delivery (e.g., reports, deliverables)
Export VAT Rebate Application Form (for goods) or Zero-Rating Declaration (for services)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA conducts rigorous audits on export zero-rating claims. If documentation is incomplete or fraudulent, the tax authority will claw back the zero-rated VAT refund, impose a penalty of 50% to 5 times the tax evaded, and levy a late payment surcharge of 0.05% per day. In cases of deliberate fraud, criminal liability may be pursued under the Criminal Law (Article 204) for tax evasion, with imprisonment up to 7 years. Additionally, the entity's export tax rebate qualification may be suspended for up to 3 years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) and State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The People's Republic of China maintains a managed floating exchange rate regime with strict separation between current account and capital account convertibility. Current account transactions, including trade in goods, services, and profit remittances by foreign-invested enterprises, are generally freely convertible provided that genuine commercial documentation is submitted to the designated foreign exchange bank and the transaction is recorded in the SAFE Foreign Exchange Account System. Capital account items, however, remain subject to prior approval, filing, or quota-based administration. A Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture established in mainland China under the Foreign Investment Law must register its foreign exchange capital via the SAFE capital project information system, and the actual receipt of foreign currency capital into a Capital Account (Foreign Currency) requires bank verification against the foreign investment certificate and the Articles of Association. For operational foreign currency needs, the JV may open a Basic Operational Currency Account, but large cross-border shareholder loans and equity injections are separately monitored. Profit repatriation to the Taiwanese shareholder is permitted only after annual statutory audit and tax clearance certificates, and the corporate income tax final settlement must be completed. The remitting bank will require the board resolution declaring dividends, the audited financial statements, the tax payment proof, and a SAFE-designated purpose code, typically 621101 for profits. Surrender requirements apply to export receipts: SAFE mandates that export proceeds in foreign currency be either repatriated into China and converted into CNY via the onshore market or retained in a domestic foreign currency current account, subject to a time limit of 180 days from the date of settlement of the export declaration unless extended under SAFE's trade facilitation measures. Non-trade current account receipts may be converted with appropriate supporting documents. Overall, the currency is not freely floating internationally, and the offshore New Taiwan Dollar is not a directly deliverable currency in mainland China; therefore cross-border flows between Taiwan and mainland China often route through USD or CNY settlement mechanisms such as the cross-strait RMB clearing line, with the Taipei and Shanghai clearing banks acting as intermediaries.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export foreign currency receipts must be repatriated to China within 180 days from the date of export declaration settlement, and under the prevailing SAFE regime there is no mandatory forced conversion ratio; however, the foreign currency retained in a domestic foreign currency account must be converted to CNY if so elected, otherwise it must be held for permitted operational or capital expenditures.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of China (Hong Kong) Limited acting as cross-border clearing participant; domestic anchor: Bank of China Limited, Shanghai Branch
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Capital Account - Foreign Currency)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (ICBC), Shanghai Pilot Free Trade Zone Branch
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account (CNY current account and foreign currency supplementary account)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: China Construction Bank (CCB), Beijing or Shanghai Branch
Agricultural Bank of China (ABC), Taiwan-Business Service Center Branch

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore fintech EMIs such as Airwallex, Payoneer, or Revolut Business are not permitted to act as the primary transactional bank account for a mainland China registered Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture because China's banking regulations require entities to maintain RMB and foreign currency accounts with domestic licensed banks that are integrated with SAFE's cross-border receipt and payment monitoring system. Digital EMIs may only serve as ancillary collection tools for overseas customers, but they cannot serve as the main clearing rail for capital injection, export proceeds repatriation, or corporate tax and dividend remittances. Legal constraints arise from the State Administration of Foreign Exchange's Circular on Further Simplifying and Optimizing Foreign Exchange Management Policies for Cross-Border Trade and Investment, which requires banks to verify the authenticity of cross-border receipts and payments directly from account transaction logs and customs declarations; such verification cannot be completed through an unregulated third-party EMI. Therefore, the viability rating is LOW for primary treasury function and MEDIUM as a supplementary receivable channel for low-value consulting fees, subject to periodic reconciliation and prompt sweep into a licensed domestic bank account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Statutory legal representative and at least one beneficial owner holding 25% or more equity interest must appear physically in-branch at the time of corporate account opening, unless the entity qualifies for the streamlined free-trade-zone electronic registration with a remote video interview and consular notarized power of attorney. In practice, Chinese commercial banks require the physical presence of the legal representative in China for first-time direct account opening; remote opening may only proceed if the bank has an offshore branch or correspondent relationship with a Taiwanese bank and the authorization is certified by the Taipei Economic and Cultural Office or a qualified notary public, plus apostille or legalization if required.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner is a Taiwan-registered entity or Taiwan resident, creating cross-strait beneficial ownership complexity and potential sanctions-screening ambiguity due to dual ISO country codes and unofficial diplomatic relations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A complete UBO declaration mapping the Taiwan shareholder chain, certified copy of the Taiwan company registration and Articles of Incorporation with English translation, passport or national ID of all natural-person shareholders holding over 25%, a notarized ownership chart showing no PRC resident individual or sanctioned person, and a letter from the Taiwan shareholder confirming the source of funds and the business rationale for the China JV, together with a confirmation that no funds originate from prohibited industries such as munitions, gambling, or virtual assets.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business scope includes 'International Tax Structuring and Transfer Pricing Advisory', which is a specified-risk professional service that may be perceived as a vehicle for tax evasion or aggressive tax avoidance, even though the tax classification is an ordinary consulting company.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A copy of the business license with the approved scope and the Ministry of Finance or tax authority licensing certificate; a detailed service agreement with an arm's length fee schedule; a written transfer pricing policy compliant with China's OECD-aligned documentation requirements; a sample engagement letter and tax structuring deliverable showing full compliance with the General Anti-Avoidance Rule; and a letter from the JV's tax advisor confirming that no service is designed to evade mainland China tax or Taiwanese tax.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The entity is a newly established Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture with low paid-in capital and no significant operational history, creating a red flag for shell-company formation or cross-border money laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A bank-certified capital injection proof showing that the minimum registered capital was contributed via a compliant cross-border wire with a proper SAFE capital verification; a three-year business plan and cash flow forecast for the management consulting and tax advisory services; a physical office lease with rent receipts or property ownership certificate; the resumes and employment contracts of the local professional staff; and a powerful tax authority registration certificate showing that the JV is an actual functioning enterprise rather than a shell.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payment rails include both Bank_Wire and Credit_Card, and the entity may receive inbound fees from multiple countries, causing concern under China's requirements for transaction authenticity verification and anti-evasion of foreign exchange settlement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A standardized fee-collection policy and a clause in the standard client engagement agreement that all fees must be paid from the client's own bank account; a list of expected counterparties with their KYC profiles and source-of-funds declarations; a month-by-month projected revenue ledger; a sample invoice and payment receipt demonstrating a logical trail to the consulting service; and a signed commitment to submit every cross-border receipt above RMB 100,000 to the designated bank with supporting underlying documents under SAFE's authenticity rules.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The Taiwan shareholder must remit registered capital from a Taiwanese bank in New Taiwan Dollars or US Dollars to the JV's Capital Account (Foreign Currency) at a designated mainland domestic bank via SWIFT MT103. The wire instruction must include the SAFE foreign exchange capital injection purpose code, typically 'Service trade contract' for consulting projects or 'Real investment (registered capital)' under SAFE's current account and capital account classification; the remitter must state the relationship to the beneficiary and the investment nature. The Chinese receiving bank will verify the Foreign Investment Information Report with the Ministry of Commerce and the SAFE foreign investment registration; then it will convert the funds into CNY at the spot rate using the onshore CNY wholesale reference price published by the China Foreign Exchange Trade System, and deposit into the RMB capital account. The bank will issue a capital verification report for the JV, which must be filed with the tax authority for stamp duty paid on registered capital. For each drawdown, the JV must update the SAFE capital project information system before the funds can be used for business purposes. The injection must not be fragmented into multiple small wires without matching investment contracts because the bank will aggregate and review all capital account receipts.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlement for consulting and tax structuring services is primarily executed through direct SWIFT MT103 payments from clients or through the JV's own outbound wire using purpose code 619 for professional consulting services. For larger procurements of software tools or overseas subcontracting, the JV may use Commercial Letters of Credit (L/C at sight) with the domestic bank as issuing bank and a foreign bank as advising and negotiating bank; however, for advisory services, Documentary Collections are less common and only suitable for physical deliverables, so the recommended rail is a clean SWIFT MT103 with an underlying signed invoice and service acceptance certificate. Cross-strait to Taiwan suppliers can also use the RMB clearing rail through Bank of China Taipei Branch and the Taipei RMB clearing house, reducing FX conversion costs for payments denominated in CNH or CNY, provided the Taiwanese counterpart maintains a RMB deposit account with a participating bank.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: SAFE-listed ordinary forward contracts between the domestic bank and the JV for hedging underlying current account receipts and payments denominated in USD or EUR for up to 12 months, with requirement of real trade background and no net speculative positions

Non-deliverable forwards on USD/CNY and EUR/CNY permitted only where the JV demonstrates a genuine exposure from a signed services export contract and the hedge is executed with a domestic bank onshore under SAFE's macro-prudential risk management guidelines

Currency swaps between USD and CNY are permissible only for capital account transactions such as foreign currency loan conversion or long-term equity repatriation, subject to SAFE approval and the underlying real investment transaction, and cannot be used for speculative arbitrage

FX options are restricted but may be permitted for hedging premium risk on commercial tenders if the JV qualifies under SAFE's products eligibility and obtains bank approval with a documented underwriting file

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Settlement Return (annual income tax return) and unappropriated earnings surtax filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau (Ministry of Finance) of the company's registration district
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by May 31 following the calendar fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing surcharge of 3% of underpaid tax for every 2 days of delay up to 15%, plus statutory interest; account freeze and compulsory collection after continued default; no direct strike-off for tax delinquency but repeated non-compliance subjects the responsible officer to fines and enforcement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholders' meeting minutes and approved financial statements registered with the company registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department of Commercial Affairs, Ministry of Economic Affairs (regional company registration office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual general meeting must be held by June 30; minutes and financial statements must be filed within 15 days after the meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Responsible officer liable to administrative fine of NT$10,000-50,000 per infraction; continuous failure may trigger MOEA order to dissolve the company (administrative strike-off).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual operation survey of foreign/Mainland China-invested enterprise (business status questionnaire issued by the Investment Commission)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed within one month of questionnaire issuance, typically issued in June of each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to respond may result in an official warning; consequential non-compliance may affect future investment applications and visa/business approval renewals.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Withholding tax statement and other annual withholding declarations (forms 107/109) for salaries and payments, delivered to tax authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau of the company's registration district
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by January 31 following the calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Surcharge and punishment scale up to 5% of unreported amounts; a pattern of repeated failure can trigger enhanced audit and eventual administrative collection enforcement.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory CPA audit and certification of annual financial statements when paid-in capital exceeds NT$30 million (approx. USD 1 million), when annual revenue exceeds NT$300 million, or when prescribed by the competent authority; public and listed companies always audited
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Taiwan IFRS (TIFRS) for companies within the audit threshold; otherwise the Enterprise Accounting Standards (EAS, local GAAP) as permitted; financial statements must conform to Business Entity Accounting Act

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Since January 1, 2024, the former annual major-shareholder filing (Company Act Art. 22-1) is abolished; the company must maintain an internal register of ultimate beneficial owners and senior officers per the Money Laundering Control Act and review/confirm it at least annually or on any shareholding transfer or ownership change; registers must be produced to supervisory agencies upon demand
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (shareholders' meeting and board minutes)
